experiment: Strict fixed-origin non-overlapping pre-retrieval aggregation at 60 m (8 native bins) and 120 m (16 native bins), retaining each block's own productive method-v4 boundary by mapping it to the containing coarse cell. Compare the aggregated KFS Monte Carlo result to the corresponding coarse representation of persisted native-grid method-v4 aerosol backscatter over 0.6-6 km. Independent and fully-correlated-within-aggregate source-error amplitudes remain separate.

implementation_anchor.interpretation: The offline KFS implementation exactly reproduces persisted method-v4 block aerosol backscatter before aggregation.

interpretation: At the existing productive boundary, 60/120 m aggregation removes the native weak-bin path fragility for every already-successful campaign block under both error-amplitude bounds.

That support gain is not lower-column neutral. The campaign median lower-column difference is already about 5% for 60 m and the 95th percentile is about 20%; integrated-column changes are also material and event dependent.
The real-data behavior does not uniformly satisfy the current loose 5% synthetic R&D preservation guard.
decision: Do not promote 60 m or 120 m aggregation as a productive support fix. Lower-column preservation must be an explicit gate, not inferred from improved completeness.
